::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Jan 2d 1892  
**From:** Elderfield Otterbourne Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University Parrish Collection
:::

Sir
I think the books I most enjoyed in early childhood were Miss Edgeworth’s series of [Early Lessons](other_books/otherbook_652.qmd), Frank, Rosamond and Harry and Lucy.

Mrs Whately’s [Fairfax family](other_books/otherbook_653.qmd)
[Anna Ross](other_books/otherbook_654.qmd) -
Miss Strickland’s [Rival Crusoes](other_books/otherbook_655.qmd)

Also very early 
Scott’s Poems<sup>1</sup> 
[Tales of A Grandfather](other_books/otherbook_656.qmd)
[The Talisman](other_books/otherbook_661.qmd)
[Ivanhoe](other_books/otherbook_657.qmd)
[Robinson Crusoe](other_books/otherbook_658.qmd)
Lamb’s [Mrs Leicesters School](other_books/otherbook_660.qmd)
[Tales from Shakespeare](other_books/otherbook_659.qmd)

This is all I can recollect of really standard books, which I read when very young

Yours truly
C M Yonge
